Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleMedia Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you require operator assistance during the call, please press star then zero on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleMedia Corp's Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We exceeded expectations in several key areas, delivering strong operational momentum across our telecom and media businesses. First, our subscriber growth was outstanding, with net additions totaling 1.2 million across residential and business segments. Second, our network investments, particularly in 5G, are yielding impressive returns. Third, fiber buildout continues to accelerate, expanding our footprint and driving adoption. Fourth, we're maintaining robust financial discipline, with EBITDA margins trending higher. Finally, we're committed to shareholder value through sustainable dividends and returns.

We're seeing very positive results from our investments in 5G Standalone core and fiber expansions, and their impact on ARPU and customer retention is significant. We've focused on scale-to-win strategies that position us ahead in coverage and efficiency. Our fiber deployments are proving successful in high-growth markets. And we're strategically positioning ourselves for converged telecom-media growth, leveraging synergies like low-latency streaming on our MediaStream platform.

I'll now turn it over to Maria for a deeper dive into our financials.

Maria Chen: Thank you, Alex. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $8.2 billion, up 6% year-over-year, driven by postpaid wireless ARPU expansion, fiber broadband ramps, and media bundle attachments. Our adjusted EBITDA was $3.1 billion, resulting in a margin of 38%, up 210 basis points from last year. We are maintaining strict cost discipline, with opex leverage from AI-driven efficiencies and a favorable mix shift toward high-margin enterprise 5G and FWA services. Capital expenditures were $1.8 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion, bringing year-to-date capex to $11.2 billion—on track for our full-year guidance of $15.5 to $16.5 billion.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our network investments, with a particular focus on 5G deployment progress and our capital expenditure profile. As you know, our network is the backbone of our integrated telecom and media strategy—delivering not just connectivity but immersive experiences like ultra-HD streaming, cloud gaming, and AR/VR content through our MediaStream platform. This $1.8 billion in Q3 capex reflects a 12% year-over-year increase, but with improving efficiency, our capex intensity—capex as a percentage of revenue—held steady at 22%, down from 24% last year.

Let me break this down. Of our total capex, approximately 65% or $1.2 billion in Q3 went toward our 5G Standalone core and radio access network upgrades, with the balance split between fiber backhaul densification at 20%, fixed wireless access customer premises equipment at 10%, and maintenance capex at 5%. This disciplined allocation reflects our scale-to-win strategy: prioritizing high-ROI 5G layers while leveraging Open RAN to reduce vendor lock-in and long-term costs by 15-20% compared to traditional deployments.

We're making accelerated progress on 5G, now reaching key inflection points that position us ahead of peers like Verizon and AT&T in mid-band coverage, while closing the gap with T-Mobile's sub-6GHz leadership. As of quarter-end, we've achieved 92% 5G coverage across our 250 million population footprint in the U.S., up from 78% a year ago. This includes 88% sub-6GHz coverage, primarily C-band at 3.7-3.98 GHz following our $2.1 billion FCC auction win in 2021, and 55% mmWave coverage in top-100 metros—expanded via dynamic spectrum sharing with our 4G LTE assets.

We've upgraded over 45,000 5G sites to Massive MIMO with 64T64R configurations, delivering peak downlink speeds of 2.5 Gbps and uplink of 300 Mbps. In Q3 alone, we lit up 8,500 new small cells in high-density urban corridors like NYC, LA, and Chicago, partnering with Ericsson for our n78 band deployments and Nokia for ORAN-compliant radios in rural markets. Our Standalone 5G core now supports 100% of our traffic, with slicing for enterprise private networks live in 15 major markets. This enables ultra-reliable low-latency communication for industrial IoT, where we've secured pilots with Ford and GE for factory automation.

Technically, we're pushing boundaries with carrier aggregation up to 200 MHz bandwidths, integrating AI-driven beamforming for 30% better spectral efficiency, and deploying O-RAN Alliance-compliant architectures on 25% of new sites. This not only cuts capex per site by 18% but future-proofs us for 6G R&D. On the media side, 5G network slicing is optimizing our MediaStream delivery—reducing latency to under 10ms for 8K live sports streaming and cloud gaming partnerships with Xbox Cloud and NVIDIA GeForce Now, driving a 15% quarter-over-quarter uplift in video ARPU.

Our progress varies by region, tailored to local dynamics. In the U.S., which accounts for 85% of capex, we're leading with 95% sub-6GHz coverage in the Northeast and West Coast. C-band rollout is complete in 40 DMAs, fueling FWA growth—we've connected 1.2 million households at $60/month, capturing 25% market share in underserved suburbs and chipping away at cable incumbents like Comcast. In Europe, at 10% of capex, our joint venture with Vodafone in the UK and Germany has hit 85% coverage, leveraging mmWave for stadiums and arenas. Recent 3.6 GHz spectrum harmonization has accelerated SA deployments, with edge computing nodes co-located for media edge caching—critical for UEFA Champions League broadcasts. In Asia-Pacific, 5% of capex through partnerships with Singtel in Southeast Asia has delivered 90% coverage in Singapore and Indonesia urban areas, focusing on FWA for SMEs, while mitigating China Mobile's dominance by emphasizing private 5G for manufacturing hubs.

Challenges persist: supply chain headwinds on RF components added $150 million to Q3 costs, but our diversified vendor mix—Ericsson 45%, Nokia 35%, Samsung 20%—mitigated impacts. Permitting delays in rural U.S. slowed small cell rollout by 10%, but federal BEAD funding, the $42 billion program, positions us for $500 million in reimbursements next year.

Strategically, 5G is our growth engine: Q3 5G traffic mix hit 52%, up 200 basis points quarter-over-quarter, correlating to a 4% ARPU uplift from premium plans like our $10/month 5G+ add-on. Enterprise 5G revenues surged 35% year-over-year to $450 million, driven by private networks for logistics like UPS drone delivery and media production with virtual studios for Disney. FWA is a standout, with 450,000 net adds and payback under 12 months at 40% gross margins—faster than wireline due to opex savings.

Looking ahead, we expect 5G capex to peak at 70% of total in FY24 before tapering to 50% in FY25 as returns compound. Our IRR on 5G investments is tracking at 22%, above our 18% hurdle, fueled by IoT adoption projected at 15 million connections by year-end 2024 and media synergies—low-latency 5G is key to our metaverse play with Meta. For Q4, we guide $4.0-4.3 billion total capex, with 5G coverage hitting 95% U.S. population.

As we continue executing on our multi-year Fiber Forward strategy, I'd like to dive deep into our fiber buildout progress, coverage expansion, and customer adoption metrics. Fiber remains the crown jewel of our network transformation, delivering symmetric multi-gigabit speeds that not only future-proof our infrastructure but also drive superior economics through higher ARPU, lower churn, and scalable media delivery capabilities.

In Q3, we deployed an additional 4,200 route miles of fiber optic cable, bringing our year-to-date total to 8,100 miles—ahead of our internal cadence for the full-year target of 16,000 miles. This includes aggressive splicing and activation in high-density corridors, where we've achieved 95%+ as-built accuracy against our engineering plans. We're now 65% through our nationwide GPON-to-XGS-PON upgrade program, with over 1.2 million homes now provisioned for 10G symmetric speeds. This aligns with the industry shift toward 10G PON standards, mirroring deployments by peers like Verizon Fios and AT&T Fiber. We've also integrated OLT disaggregation via partnerships with Nokia and Adtran, reducing capex per foot by 18% quarter-over-quarter through software-defined networking efficiencies.

Capex for fiber in Q3 came in at $285 million, within our guided range, with a forward-looking ROIC trajectory improving to 12-15% in mature footprints as depreciation stabilizes. We're leveraging $450 million in RDOF disbursements to date and expect an additional $1.2 billion from BEAD Phase 1 awards in Q4, primarily targeting our unserved rural expansions.

Turning to coverage expansion, our homes-passed metric is the clearest indicator of our footprint growth. We passed 3.2 million homes by quarter-end, up 28% year-over-year from 2.5 million at the start of 2024. This represents a sequential add of 450,000 homes in Q3 alone, with 60% in greenfield builds and 40% from densification in existing clusters.

Regionally, performance was strong: Sunbelt markets like Florida, Texas, and Georgia—our largest cluster at 1.1 million homes passed—saw 35% year-over-year growth, fueled by population in-migration and partnerships with homebuilders like Lennar for pre-wiring new developments. Take rates here are hitting 32%, above our network average. Midwest expansion in Ohio, Indiana, and Michigan added 180,000 homes passed, supported by $120 million in CAF II subsidies—this region is pivotal for margin expansion as fiber economics scale quickly in mid-tier density markets. Northeast push in Pennsylvania and New Jersey reached 650,000 homes passed, where we're directly competing with Verizon's Fios footprint and have captured 15% market share in overlapping ZIPs through aggressive pricing on our 2Gig/2Gig tiers. Rural initiatives passed 120,000 homes in unserved counties, aligning with NTIA goals and positioning us for middle-mile grants.

We're on track for 5 million homes passed by year-end 2024, accelerating into 2025 with 2.5 million more via M&A tuck-ins, like our recent $300 million acquisition of a 400,000-home regional MSO in the Carolinas.

Customer adoption is where the story gets even more compelling. Fiber broadband subscribers grew to 825,000 by quarter-end, adding 165,000 in Q3—a record quarterly net add and up 45% year-over-year. This translates to an overall take rate of 25.8% on homes passed, expanding 300 basis points sequentially. In markets over 24 months vintage, take rates exceed 35%, with quarterly ramp-up curves consistently outperforming industry benchmarks from USTelecom data.

Driving this adoption: pricing and packaging, where our fiber ARPU hit $112, up 9% year-over-year, anchored by 71% penetration of multi-gig tiers at 1Gig+. Bundles with our WatchWave streaming service—now featuring exclusive FAST channels and Peacock integration via our NBCU carriage deal—boosted attachment rates to 42%. Marketing ROI from digital lead gen via Google Fiber-like retargeting yielded a 4.2x CAC payback in under 6 months. Churn dynamics saw fiber churn fall to 0.9% monthly recurring revenue, versus 1.8% on legacy HFC/DOCSIS, enabling 200 basis points EBITDA margin lift in fiber-heavy markets.

Strategically, this positions us uniquely in a consolidating industry. Unlike cable peers like Comcast or Charter, whose DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades cap out at asymmetric 10G down/1-2G up, our all-fiber plant delivers true symmetry and lower latency for cloud gaming, AR/VR media, and enterprise backhaul—key for 5G small-cell densification. We've already backhauled 2,500 C-band sites for our wireless JV partner, generating $45 million in new revenue.

Looking forward, Q4 guidance calls for 500,000 homes passed and 180,000 subscriber adds, with take rates trending to 27%. Risks include permitting delays in Northeast metros and supply chain for 10G pluggables, but our $2.8 billion liquidity and vendor pre-pays mitigate these. Fiber isn't just a network—it's our path to 40%+ EBITDA margins by 2027 and leadership in the converged telecom-media ecosystem.

Before diving deeper into the financials, I'd like to spend some time on our core subscriber growth metrics, as these remain the lifeblood of our telecommunications and media business. Net subscriber additions across our residential and business segments totaled 1.2 million in the quarter, marking our strongest quarterly performance since Q4 2021 and representing a 28% year-over-year increase. This momentum underscores the success of our Connect Everywhere strategy, which leverages our nationwide 5G Standalone network, aggressive fiber-to-the-premises deployments, and bundled media offerings.

Residential drove the lion's share at 982,000 net new subscribers—up 32% year-over-year and accelerating from Q2. Within residential, we saw balanced growth across broadband, wireless, and video/streaming, fueled by our fixed wireless access ramp-up and promotional pricing on NovaStream+ bundles.

Residential broadband added 456,000 net subscribers, a 41% year-over-year surge. Fiber broadband was the star, with 312,000 net adds—our best-ever quarter—bringing our total FTTP footprint to 28 million homes passed, up 22% year-over-year. This reflects over $1.2 billion invested in 2023-2024 to expand our XGS-PON network in the Northeast and Sunbelt markets, where we've achieved 65% take rates in mature nodes. Hybrid fiber-coax DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades contributed another 112,000 adds, particularly in legacy territories competing head-on with Comcast's Xfinity 10G rollout. FWA broadband, powered by our mmWave and C-band 5G spectrum, exploded to 32,000 net adds—more than double the prior quarter—targeting rural underserved areas akin to T-Mobile's successful FWA playbook. Churn held steady at 1.1%, below industry averages per New Street Research benchmarks, thanks to our AI-driven retention tools that predict and preempt voluntary disconnects with personalized upsell offers.

Residential wireless postpaid mobile net adds reached 421,000, up 25% year-over-year, with smartphone adds at 378,000 and connected device adds like tablets and wearables at 43,000. Our 5G SA core, now covering 85% of our 110 million postpaid base, has been a game-changer, enabling low-latency services like AR/VR streaming partnerships with Meta. We captured market share from Verizon and AT&T through our Unlimited Max plan at $70/month, bundled with NovaStream, which saw 15% higher adoption in promotional markets. Prepaid wireless added 65,000 nets, driven by ethnic marketing in Hispanic and Asian communities, where we grew 18% year-over-year amid intensifying competition from MVNOs like Mint Mobile. Overall residential wireless ARPU rose 2.3% to $52.40, reflecting successful migrations to 5G plans.

Residential video/streaming net adds were 105,000, reversing prior cord-cutting trends with our NovaStream platform—our DTC streaming service aggregating Peacock, Paramount+, and our linear cable channels. This quarter's 22% year-over-year growth came from deep integrations with our broadband gateway, achieving 45% penetration among new fiber customers. Regionally, the Southeast led with 42% of adds, where hurricane recovery efforts boosted FWA video bundles.

Shifting to business, we delivered 218,000 net adds—a robust 12% year-over-year increase and our third straight quarter of acceleration. This segment now represents 24% of total revenue, with EBITDA margins expanding 150 basis points to 52%, thanks to higher-value enterprise wins.

SMB added 142,000 nets, up 15% year-over-year, primarily from SD-WAN and hosted VoIP solutions. Our NovaBiz Essentials bundle, priced at $99/month for 1Gbps fiber with Microsoft 365 integration, resonated in suburban markets, adding 89,000 broadband lines. We've outpaced Spectrum Enterprise in this tier by emphasizing our 99.999% uptime SLA, verified by independent audits.

Enterprise added 76,000 nets, highlighted by 12,000 primary 100G+ wavelength connections for hyperscalers like AWS and Google Cloud. Our dark fiber deals in data center hubs like Ashburn, VA, and Phoenix, AZ, drove 28% of enterprise growth, capitalizing on AI-driven bandwidth demand—a trend echoed in recent Lumen and Zayo earnings. Private 5G campus networks added 4,200 sites for manufacturing clients like automotive plants in the Midwest, leveraging our CBRS spectrum holdings. Churn was a pristine 0.8%, bolstered by multi-year contracts averaging 48 months.

Regionally, the U.S. Sunbelt—Florida, Texas, Arizona—accounted for 38% of total net adds, up from 29% last year, driven by population in-migration and our $800 million capex allocation to FTTP overbuilds against Frontier's asset-light model. The Midwest lagged at 22% due to seasonal construction delays but showed promise with FWA pilots mirroring Starlink's rural penetration. Internationally, our media arm in Latin America via a 40% stake in Claro Brasil contributed 15,000 net mobile adds amid 5G auctions.

Strategically, these results validate our pivot to converged services: 68% of residential net adds took multi-play bundles, lifting blended ARPU 4% year-over-year to $148. We've initiated technical roadmaps like Open RAN trials with Nokia in 12 markets to cut opex by 20% long-term, and edge computing partnerships with Akamai for low-latency media delivery. Competitively, we're gaining ground on the Big Three—our postpaid phone market share hit 28.5% per Carrier Intelligence—while fending off cablecos via superior fiber economics at 1.8x ROI versus HFC.

Looking forward, we guide to 4.8-5.2 million full-year net adds, implying Q4 at about 1.3 million, supported by back-to-school promos and NFL season streaming tie-ins. Our network remains the industry's most awarded for 5G speed per Ookla Q3 2024, positioning us for sustained share gains.

As we wrap up a transformative quarter, I'm pleased to provide our forward-looking guidance on EBITDA margins, a core metric that underscores our operational leverage in both telecom and media segments. For context, our trailing twelve-month EBITDA margin stood at 37.2% this quarter, up 210 basis points year-over-year, driven by disciplined cost controls and a favorable revenue mix shift toward high-margin 5G enterprise services and bundled streaming offerings.

Looking ahead, we are guiding to an EBITDA margin of 38% to 40% for Q4, with full-year FY25 guidance in the range of 39% to 42%. This represents approximately 150 to 300 basis points of expansion at the midpoint compared to FY24, positioning us at the upper end of telecom/media peers like Verizon and Comcast, who are targeting mid-40s over the longer term.

Key drivers start with tailwinds from network modernization initiatives yielding significant efficiencies. We've accelerated our Open RAN deployment across 40% of our U.S. macro sites in partnership with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony, reducing total cost of ownership by 15-20% through RAN virtualization and disaggregated architectures. This is complemented by our FWA ramp-up, where we've added 1.2 million subscribers year-over-year—mirroring T-Mobile's success but with our media bundling edge—shifting mix to 25% of broadband revenue from low-capex FWA, which boasts EBITDA margins north of 60%.

On the media side, synergies from our NexaStream platform are accretive. Post our Disney+-Hulu bundle integration, ARPU uplift from video-telecom convergence has hit $18.50, up 8% year-over-year, with ad-tier adoption at 35% of new subs—think Paramount+ with Showtime's model but hyper-localized. We're forecasting media segment margins to expand to 45% in FY25, offsetting any near-term OTT price compression from Netflix's password crackdown.

Regionally, our guidance embeds U.S. performance at 41-43% margins, fueled by C-band spectrum utilization exceeding 70% in key markets and enterprise private 5G deals with Fortune 500 clients like manufacturing verticals using our edge computing slices—similar to AT&T's FirstNet momentum. In Europe, where we've divested non-core assets in Germany akin to Vodafone's tower sales, margins should hit 37-39%, buoyed by EU gigabit broadband subsidies under the Digital Decade targets, though tempered by Ofcom-like regulatory fees up 5% on inflation. Asia-Pacific, our growth engine at 20% of revenue, guides to 35-37% amid 5G SA core rollout in India and Indonesia, where Jio-like pricing discipline and towerco partnerships like with Indus Towers analogs mitigate competitive intensity from Reliance and Singtel.

This margin expansion is anchored in three pillars: opex leverage, where SG&A as a percentage of revenue drops to 22% via AI-powered network orchestration—reducing field maintenance costs by 12% through predictive analytics from our Ericsson OSS integration; capex efficiency, guiding to 16-18% of revenue in FY25 down from 20% this year as 5G capex peaks and we pivot to software-defined networking; and revenue quality, with postpaid wireless at 92% of mobile revenue and enterprise up 25% year-over-year on IoT and 5G-xHaul services.

Headwinds remain: energy costs for our 5G densification are up 10% amid global inflation, partially offset by green energy PPAs covering 30% of our footprint. Rural broadband competition from Starlink and EchoStar's Dish Network could pressure FWA take rates by 5-10% in underserved U.S. markets, and spectrum auction fees in Europe—post the ongoing 6GHz WRC-23 debates—add about $200 million in FY25 opex. We've baked conservatism into our guide, assuming 2-3% broadband cord-cutting acceleration.

Overall, this guidance reflects our Margin First playbook: ruthless prioritization of ROI-positive investments, like our $1.5 billion share repurchase this year, while scaling next-gen services. We remain committed to free cash flow conversion above 50% and dividend growth, targeting a 3.5% yield.

As we wrap up, I'd like to dive deep into our commitment to shareholder returns, with a particular focus on dividend sustainability and the dollar value we're delivering. In an industry where capex intensity for 5G spectrum deployment, fiber-to-the-home rollouts, and streaming content investments can pressure free cash flow, we've engineered a returns framework that's both robust and flexible.

First, our headline dividend metrics: we declared a quarterly dividend of $0.52 per share earlier this month, marking a 4% increase year-over-year and our 18th consecutive quarter of growth. This translates to an annualized dividend of $2.08 per share, yielding approximately 4.6% at current trading levels—positioning us at the high end of our telecom-media peer set, ahead of Verizon's 6.5% yield but with superior growth prospects compared to AT&T's more stagnant profile post its WarnerMedia divestiture.

Sustainability starts with coverage, and we're firing on all cylinders. Our trailing 12-month free cash flow reached $11.2 billion, up 12% year-over-year, driven by 5G postpaid ARPU expansion to $58.40—our highest ever—fueled by premium unlimited plans bundled with our WaveStream+ video service, now at 28 million domestic subscribers. This FCF fully covers our $5.1 billion annual dividend obligation more than 2.2x, with a payout ratio of just 46% of FCF. That's healthier than Comcast's 55% ratio amid its Peacock streaming ramp-up or Charter's 62% as it chases rural broadband density.

Leverage is another pillar: our net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA stands at 2.6x, down from 2.9x a year ago, thanks to $3.2 billion in deleveraging from asset sales like our underperforming tower portfolio to American Tower. This gives us ample headroom under our 3.5x target covenant, even as we navigate C-band spectrum amortization from the 2021 FCC auction. Capex, which peaked at 18% of revenue in 2023 for Open RAN trials and 400G fiber upgrades, is now trending down to 15% in 2025 as 5G coverage hits 98% in our U.S. footprint, mirroring T-Mobile's efficiency playbook but with our media synergies.

On total shareholder returns, we're delivering $8.7 billion in dollar value this year, a 15% increase from 2023. That breaks down to $5.1 billion in dividends and $3.6 billion in share repurchases under our $10 billion authorization, retiring 4.1% of shares outstanding at an average price of $42. We've opportunistically bought back during 10% year-to-date dips tied to macro rate fears, enhancing EPS accretion by 7 cents per share. Our total shareholder yield now clocks in at 8.2%, outpacing the S&P 500 Telecom Index's 6.1% and even edging Disney's 4.8% amid its Hulu linear TV unwind.

Regionally, this returns engine is diversified: in North America, driving 72% of FCF, U.S. wireless churn held at a stellar 0.82%, bolstered by FWA onboarding 1.2 million households—directly competing with Starlink in rural markets. Europe, at 18% of FCF, saw dividend-equivalent returns via our Vodafone JV in Germany, where 5G SA core deployment lifted EBITDA margins to 42%, enabling a €500 million special payout. In Latin America, our media assets like the Claro Video platform grew ad revenue 22% year-over-year on telenovela originals and sports rights, funding local buybacks without straining the corporate balance sheet. Challenges persist in APAC, where regulatory spectrum refarming in India delayed $200 million in FCF, but we're mitigating via edge computing partnerships with Nokia for low-latency gaming streams.

Looking forward, our dividend sustainability is locked in through strategic levers. We've guided FY2024 FCF to $11.5-$12.0 billion, implying 2.3x-2.4x coverage even if capex stays flat. For 2025, expect mid-single-digit dividend growth, supported by FCF yield expansion to 9% as 5G opex efficiencies like AI-driven network slicing reduce energy costs 15%, offsetting streaming content capex capped at $2.8 billion via targeted originals like our NexFlix exclusives. M&A remains opportunistic—think bolt-on fiber deals like our recent $1.2 billion acquisition of a Midwest MSO, echoing Frontier's Ziply pivot—while maintaining buyback authorization at $7 billion remaining.

In summary, at TeleMedia, shareholder returns aren't a residual; they're core to our DNA. With $2.08 annual dividend, 2.2x FCF coverage, and $8.7 billion total dollar value this year, we're delivering telecom-grade reliability with media upside.

Dr. Raj Patel: Thank you, Maria. I would like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage to 92% of our U.S. footprint, with key upgrades in Massive MIMO and small cells enhancing speeds and reliability. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, with uptime exceeding 99.999% in core markets, and we are seeing increased data usage across our customer base—5G traffic now at 52% of total. We are also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure, deploying advanced AI threat detection integrated with our O-RAN stack. Our team's dedication to Open RAN and edge computing has been instrumental in achieving these results, enabling new use cases like private networks and low-latency media delivery.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for 5G pricing?

Alex Rivera: Certainly, John. In the competitive landscape, we're gaining share against Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile through superior mid-band C-band coverage at 88% and aggressive pricing on premium 5G+ plans at $10/month add-on, bundled with MediaStream. Our strategy emphasizes FWA at $60/month to capture suburbs from Comcast, with Open RAN efficiencies allowing 15-20% lower costs. Enterprise private 5G slicing has driven 35% revenue growth, outpacing peers via pilots in IoT and logistics. We're focused on ARPU uplift while maintaining market share at 28.5% in postpaid phones.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact EBITDA margins?

Maria Chen: We anticipate 1.3 million net adds in Q4, in line with our full-year guide of 4.8-5.2 million, driven by fiber adds of 180,000, FWA ramps, and business enterprise wins. This will support EBITDA margin expansion to 38-40% in Q4 and 39-42% in FY25, as higher-margin FWA and bundles shift mix, offset by capex peak, with opex leverage from AI tools adding 150-300 bps.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

Dr. Raj Patel: Absolutely, Mike. Our fiber plans are accelerating, with 500,000 homes passed in Q4 toward 5 million by year-end, and take rates at 27%. We've deployed 8,100 YTD route miles, 65% through XGS-PON upgrades, leveraging Nokia/Adtran for 18% capex savings per foot. ROI is tracking 12-15% ROIC in mature areas, faster payback via $112 ARPU and 0.9% churn, plus backhaul revenue of $45 million from 2,500 5G sites. BEAD and RDOF add $1.65 billion in funding, enhancing returns to 1.8x versus HFC peers.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in TeleMedia Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
